facts.fact: INTIC chairman Lourino Chemane said Mozambique has completed a thorough review of the Electronic Government Systems Interoperability Regulation, which sets standards for integrating and managing public information systems; the report is dated 2025-12-05 and gives no other date.

note: carried from interoperability by its own text; no document opened

systems.system: Plataforma Comum de Comunicação de Dados do Governo e de Interoperabilidade (Plataforma Tecnológica de Interoperabilidade)
systems.country_label: Plataforma de Interoperabilidade de Governo Electrónico
systems.owner: INAGE manages it; INTIC specifies it
systems.tiers: all public administration institutions (central and local State bodies, local authorities)

note: Decree 67/2017 defines the interoperability framework as principles, standards, guidelines and architectures and tasks INTIC with proposing standards and a reference architecture, but names no set of technical standards (formats, codes, interfaces) and states none exists or is published; a mandate to write standards gives no fact, and the platform's functional specifications are an exchange platform's, so nothing for standing or use.

facts.fact: Ecofin Agency reports that Mozambique is currently revising the 2017 interoperability framework to strengthen technical standards, data-exchange governance, data protection and cybersecurity.

note: carried from interoperability by its own text; no document opened

facts.fact: INTIC's post says the proposed revision of Decree 67/2017, presented on 23 October 2026, sets out technical specifications, architecture and interoperability standards for the state's systems; it is proposed, not adopted.

INTIC chair Lourino Chemane said on 13 October 2025 that revision of Decree 67/2017 is under way, with EU support, to add technical specifications, technical data-exchange standards and a governance structure.

note: Revision in progress; no published standards or checks stated.
